module.description: Implement a module of a carry-lookahead 32-bit adder that uses the Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) architecture.

ports.output: 32-bit output representing the sum of A and B. The module name "S" is case-sensitive.
Carry-out output. The module name "C32" is case-sensitive.

module.implementation: The top module adder_32bit consists of several instances of the 16 bit CLA block <module refid="cla_16bit" />. And each <module refid="cla_16bit" /> is constructed from 4-bit CLA blocks from the <module refid="cla_4bit" />.

module.description: A module of a carry-lookahead 4-bit adder that uses the Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) architecture.

ports.output: 16-bit output representing the sum of A and B.

logic_description.description: Notice that below descriptions are along with tags <logic />. These tags <logic /> could be described more detail in the below description in the <implementation /> tag. With a <logic type="combinational_logic" />, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this <logic type="combinational_logic" /> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block. With a <logic type="sequential_logic" />, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other <logic type="sequential_logic" /> or <logic type="combinational_logic" /> states. With a <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description. With a <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation. With a <logic id="temp" /> tag with width_description and depth_description attributes declaration, such as <logic id="temp" width_description="[a:b]" depth_description="[c:d]"/>, it must be declared as `wire [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `combinational_logic`. Otherwise, the logic must be declared as `reg [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `sequential_logic` or a `combinational_logic` driven in a `alway @(*)` block.
logic_description.logic: <logic refid="p" /> is 4-bit carry propagation. Each bit of the <logic refid="p" /> is is driven by a <output refid="p_group" /> from an instance of a <module refid="cla_4bit" />.
<logic refid="g" /> is 4-bit carry generation. Each bit of the <logic refid="g" /> is is driven by a <output refid="g_group" /> from an instance of a <module refid="cla_4bit" />.
<logic refid="c" /> is 4-bit internal carry calculations. Each bit of the <logic refid="c" /> is is driven by a <output refid="cout" /> from an instance of a <module refid="cla_4bit" />.

module.implementation: Each 4 bits of <output refid="sum" /> is driven by a <output refid="sum" /> from an instance of a <module refid="cla_4bit" />. The <output refid="cout" /> is the MSB of the <logic refid="c" />.

module.description: A module of a carry-lookahead 4-bit adder that uses the Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) architecture.

ports.output: 4-bit output representing the sum of A and B.

logic_description.description: Notice that below descriptions are along with tags <logic />. These tags <logic /> could be described more detail in the below description in the <implementation /> tag. With a <logic type="combinational_logic" />, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this <logic type="combinational_logic" /> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block. With a <logic type="sequential_logic" />, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other <logic type="sequential_logic" /> or <logic type="combinational_logic" /> states. With a <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description. With a <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation. With a <logic id="temp" /> tag with width_description and depth_description attributes declaration, such as <logic id="temp" width_description="[a:b]" depth_description="[c:d]"/>, it must be declared as `wire [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `combinational_logic`. Otherwise, the logic must be declared as `reg [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `sequential_logic` or a `combinational_logic` driven in a `alway @(*)` block.
logic_description.logic: <logic refid="p" /> is 4-bit carry propagation. The 4-bit <logic refid="p" /> is bitwise-XOR result of <input refid="a" /> and <input refid="b" />.
<logic refid="g" /> is 4-bit carry generation. The 4-bit <logic refid="g" /> is bitwise-AND result of <input refid="a" /> and <input refid="b" />.

<logic refid="c" /> is 5-bit for internal carry calculations. The first bit c[0] is the <input refid="cin" />
With the rest internal bits of <logic refid="c" />, the calculation is as follows: c[1] is set to g[0] XORing with the bitwise AND of p[0] and c[0], c[2] is set to g[1] XORing with the bitwise AND of p[1] and c[1], etc, c[4] is set to g[3] XORing with the bitwise AND of p[3] and c[3].
<logic refid="p_group" /> is a propagate signal to a higher-level CLA logic circuit. <logic refid="p_group" /> is the bitwise AND operation of the 4 bits of the internal <logic refid="p" />.

<logic refid="g_group" /> is a generate signal to a higher-level CLA logic circuit. <logic refid="g_group" /> is the bitwise OR operation of the 4 elements: - The first element is the g[3]. - The second element is the bitwise AND operation of g[2] and p[3]. - The third element is the bitwise AND operation of g[1], p[3], and p[2]. - The third element is the bitwise AND operation of g[0], p[3], p[2], and p[1].

module.implementation: The <output refid="sum" /> is the bitwise XOR of the 4-bit <logic refid="p" /> and the first 4 bits of <logic refid="c" />. The carry-lookahead 4-bit adder can also be used in a higher-level circuit by having each CLA logic circuit produce a propagate <output refid="p_group" /> and generate <output refid="g_group" /> signal to a higher-level CLA logic circuit. The <output refid="cout" /> is the MSB of the <logic refid="c" />.
